title: Morocco first, then Kenya's Wild Loop
overview:
- **Dates:** LAX **Sat Dec 19** → Morocco → Nairobi → LAX **Sat Jan 16**. Christmas in Morocco; Kenya from Dec 28 is the Wild loop unchanged.
- **Stopover:** 7 nights from Marrakech over the High Atlas to the Erg Chebbi dunes (Christmas Eve in a desert camp), then north to the Middle Atlas cedar forest for Barbary macaques. Fly out from Casablanca via Cairo and land in Nairobi at about 04:55 on Dec 28.
- **Verdict:** Worth it if you want a big change of scenery and culture before Kenya: Atlas passes, kasbahs, gorges, Sahara dunes and the macaques. The wildlife is thin next to East Africa, though: apart from the macaques and camels it is mostly birds. The main drawbacks are the long Dec 27 flight day via Cairo, with no nonstop to Nairobi, and desert nights near freezing. It adds about $2,000 pp all-in over the base trip. Checked: Level 2 advisory (Sep 4 2026), visa-free entry, the AT251 Sun/Tue/Fri pattern and MS848 (daily, 13:30-20:25) are all confirmed. Changed: flagged that MS849's Cairo departure has moved between 20:55 and 23:55 during 2026 (the 20:55 slot would break the connection), corrected the Azrou-CMN distance to ~300 km, and confirmed that the budget sums (~$3,495 pp, +$1,995 vs base) and every low ≤ planned ≤ high range hold.
- **Safety:** US State Dept Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (terrorism). Advisory reissued Sep 4 2026, level unchanged.. Morocco is one of the more stable and tourist-friendly countries in Africa. The Level 2 rating reflects a general terrorism risk; terrorists may target tourist sites, transport hubs and markets. The last deadly attacks on tourists were the 2011 Marrakech cafe bombing and the 2018 killing of two hikers near Imlil. The everyday risks are petty theft, medina hustlers, and mountain driving in winter. Merzouga is close to the closed Algerian border, but the tourist dune area is routinely visited and safe.
- **Cost:** $9,595 pp, **+$1,995** vs the Wild loop alone ($7,600).

**Highlights:** Christmas Eve in an Erg Chebbi dune camp: camel trek at sunset, stars, Berber drumming, sunrise from the 150 m dunes · Barbary macaques in the Cedre Gouraud cedar forest near Azrou (the only macaque in Africa, endangered) · Crossing the High Atlas on the Tizi n'Tichka pass to the UNESCO ksar of Ait Benhaddou · Todra Gorge (300 m walls) and the Dades Valley 'road of a thousand kasbahs' · Marrakech medina, Jemaa el-Fna night market, Jardin Majorelle and Berber Museum · Desert birding around Merzouga/Dayet Srji (desert sparrow, fulvous babbler, maybe flamingos if the lake has water) · Gnawa music village of Khamlia on Christmas Day

**Drawbacks:** Weak on 'exotic wildlife' compared with Kenya: the macaques are the only real mammal highlight; fennec fox and Barbary sheep sightings are rare · Getting to Nairobi is awkward: there is no confirmed nonstop from Morocco. The best timing is EgyptAir MS848 CMN 13:30 to CAI 20:25, then MS849 to NBO. MS849 has shown both 23:55 and 20:55 Cairo departures in 2026; only the 23:55 slot connects, so verify the December timetable before booking · Dec 26 (~5h road) and Dec 27 (~3.5h road + ~13h of flights and layover) are back-to-back hard days; the Dec 28 Nairobi rest day absorbs it · Outbound Dec 19 is a Saturday, and the Royal Air Maroc LAX-CMN nonstop (AT251, 10:20 departure) only flies Sun/Tue/Fri, so you connect via Europe. The exception is leaving a day early, Fri Dec 18. Turkish via Istanbul forces an overnight in Istanbul and loses a Morocco day · Cold nights in the desert and the Middle Atlas; some budget riads and auberges have weak heating · Late December is peak European holiday season in Marrakech and Merzouga: book camps and riads now · Upgrade option: a luxury desert camp ($180-350 pp/night) and a private 4x4 with a guide add ~$400-700 pp · Cheaper option: shared 3-day Marrakech-Merzouga-Fes tours (~$190-300 pp), but they involve 9-10h drive days, which breaks the pace rule

### Then Kenya (Wild loop)
- **Route (one camping crew, all road):** Nairobi → Ol Pejeta 2n → **Samburu 3n** (NYE) → Thomson's Falls 1n → Lake Nakuru 2n → **Kakamega rainforest 2n** → Kericho 1n → **Mara conservancy 4n** → Naivasha + Hell's Gate 2n → airport hotel → fly home.
- **Exotic wildlife focus:** Samburu's Special Five + vulturine guineafowl, chimps + black rhino (Ol Pejeta), Rothschild's giraffe (Nakuru), colobus + De Brazza's monkeys + great blue turaco (Kakamega), big cats (Mara). See **Wildlife**.
- **No beach, no rental car:** crew 4x4 + driver-guide included.
- **Budget: ~$7,600 pp** (incl. flights + $300 contingency). Crew days are the cost driver.
- **Cuts:** skip Kakamega (−$800), home Jan 14 (−$450), yellow fever done (−$200), fly out of the Mara (−$90).
- **Fatigue:** max ~4.5h road/day, overnight stops split every long leg, 9 zero-travel days. Last day is a ~25h journey home.

itinerary.title: Depart LAX
itinerary.details: Afternoon flight LAX-CDG (~10.5h, overnight). Sleep on the plane.

itinerary.title: Arrive Marrakech
itinerary.details: Land CDG ~10-11:30, connect to RAK (~3.5h), arrive late afternoon. Riad pickup (~25 min). Mint tea, early night. Travel ~6h today plus yesterday's 10.5h.

itinerary.title: Rest + medina
itinerary.details: No transport. Slow morning. Jardin Majorelle + Berber Museum, souks, Ben Youssef Medersa. Sunset from a cafe terrace over Jemaa el-Fna, food stalls at night. Meet the driver for a briefing.

itinerary.title: Over the Atlas
itinerary.details: Driver 08:30. Tizi n'Tichka pass, ~4h road with stops. Afternoon walk through the Ait Benhaddou ksar, climb to the granary at sunset. Moussier's redstart on the pass.
itinerary.meals: B, L roadside tagine, D guesthouse (half board)

itinerary.title: Valley of kasbahs
itinerary.details: ~4h road: Ouarzazate, Skoura palmery, Dades Gorge switchbacks, Todra. Late-afternoon walk into the Todra Gorge (300 m walls).

itinerary.title: Christmas Eve in the dunes
itinerary.details: Morning gorge walk, then ~3h road to Merzouga. ~15:30 camel trek 1-1.5h to the camp, sunset on the dunes, dinner, drums, stars. Cold night (1-5 C).

itinerary.title: Christmas rest day
itinerary.details: Dune sunrise, camel back ~1h, then breakfast and a shower at the auberge. Lazy day. Optional: Khamlia Gnawa music, Dayet Srji lake birding (desert sparrow, flamingos if wet), afternoon nap.

itinerary.title: Cedars + macaques
itinerary.details: Depart 08:00. ~5h road: Ziz Gorges, Midelt (lunch), Azrou. ~15:00 Cedre Gouraud forest for the Barbary macaques; Levaillant's woodpecker possible. Snow possible.

itinerary.title: Long haul to Kenya
itinerary.details: Leave 07:30, ~3.5h (~300 km) to CMN airport. EgyptAir MS848 13:30 to CAI 20:25 (~5h), ~3.5h airside wait, MS849 23:55 to NBO, landing 04:55 Dec 28, then straight to the Nairobi rest day.

itinerary.title: Land + rest day
itinerary.details: Land early morning (see Route). Taxi (~20m) to guesthouse (room held from Dec 27). Sleep. Optional: Sheldrick baby elephants 11:00 ($20, ~20m away; book online now).

itinerary.title: Drive north to Ol Pejeta
itinerary.details: Crew pickup ~08:30. ~4h via Nanyuki, equator stop. Camp set at OPC campsite. PM: chimp sanctuary + sunset drive.

itinerary.title: Rhinos + Mt Kenya
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn + late drives. Black/white rhino, lion, elephant, Grevy's zebra. Optional lion tracking (~$70; not budgeted).

itinerary.title: North to Samburu + NYE by the river
itinerary.details: ~2.5–3h via Nanyuki + Isiolo; drop into hot, dry north. Camp on the Ewaso Ng'iro river. PM drive. Quiet NYE under the stars.

itinerary.title: Samburu Special Five
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn + late drives: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, gerenuk, Beisa oryx, Somali ostrich. Vulturine guineafowl, river elephants. Midday siesta (30–35°C).

itinerary.title: Leopards + river day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Search riverine forest for leopard; lions, cheetah possible. Optional Samburu village visit (~$20–30 pp, paid locally).

itinerary.title: Back to the cool highlands
itinerary.details: ~3.5h via Isiolo + Nanyuki. Thomson's Falls (74 m) walk to the bottom. Camp at the falls; cool night (fleece).

itinerary.title: Short hop to Nakuru
itinerary.details: ~1.5h downhill to Lake Nakuru NP. Camp inside the park. PM drive: rhino, Rothschild's giraffe.

itinerary.title: Nakuru day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn drive to Baboon Cliff. Black + white rhino, flamingos/pelicans (numbers vary), tree-climbing lions if lucky. Siesta.

itinerary.title: West to the rainforest
itinerary.details: ~4–4.5h via Eldoret. Rondo Retreat inside the forest, full board. Dusk walk: colobus calling.

itinerary.title: Rainforest day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn bird walk with local guide (~Ksh300–500 pp): great blue turaco, hornbills. Black-and-white colobus, De Brazza's + red-tailed monkeys. Lirhanda Hill. Optional night walk (pottos, bushbabies).

itinerary.title: Tea country
itinerary.details: ~2.5–3h via Kisumu. Tea-estate walk, factory visit. Easy afternoon.

itinerary.title: Into the Mara conservancy
itinerary.details: ~3–3.5h via Bomet + Mulot (last hour rough). Camp in Enonkishu (or Pardamat/Ol Chorro). Dusk drive.

itinerary.title: Full Mara day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Dawn + late drives, off-road, few vehicles. Big cats, plains game, newborn topi. Siesta.

itinerary.title: Maasai walk + night drive
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Morning walk with Maasai ranger. PM drive. Night drive if allowed (aardvark, bat-eared fox, genets).

itinerary.title: Extra Mara day
itinerary.details: Zero travel. Full-day drive with picnic lunch, following whatever the guides found. Sundowner.

itinerary.title: Road to Naivasha
itinerary.details: ~4–4.5h via Narok + Mai Mahiu. Lakeshore camp. Hippos at dusk.

itinerary.title: Hell's Gate + boat
itinerary.details: No long travel (30m local). Bike or walk Hell's Gate among zebra + giraffe, gorge hike. PM boat + Crescent Island walk. Rest.

itinerary.title: Airport hotel
itinerary.details: ~2.5–3h via A104 + Southern Bypass. Tip crew. Shower, repack, early night.

itinerary.title: Fly home
itinerary.details: Wake ~02:45, 10–20m to JKIA. TK608 04:50 → IST 11:45. ~2h45 airside connect. TK9 ~14:30 → LAX ~18:15 same day. ~25h door to door.

practical:
## Morocco stopover
- **Visa (US passport):** US passport: Morocco is visa-free for up to 90 days (passport must be valid 6+ months on entry; one blank page). Paris (CDG) airside transit needs no visa, and the EU EES/ETIAS systems do not apply to airside transit. Cairo transit: no Egyptian visa needed if you stay airside. Kenya eTA is still required as in the base plan, so make sure it covers a Dec 28 entry.
- **Safety — US State Dept Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (terrorism). Advisory reissued Sep 4 2026, level unchanged.:** Morocco is one of the more stable and tourist-friendly countries in Africa. The Level 2 rating reflects a general terrorism risk; terrorists may target tourist sites, transport hubs and markets. The last deadly attacks on tourists were the 2011 Marrakech cafe bombing and the 2018 killing of two hikers near Imlil. The everyday risks are petty theft, medina hustlers, and mountain driving in winter. Merzouga is close to the closed Algerian border, but the tourist dune area is routinely visited and safe.
  - Hire a licensed driver and drive in daylight only; the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m) and the Midelt road can get snow or ice in late December. Check road status the night before.
  - In the Marrakech medina, ignore 'the square is closed' and 'follow me' faux guides; agree prices before henna or photos at Jemaa el-Fna, and watch for pickpockets in crowds.
  - Do not wander east of the Erg Chebbi tourist zone toward the Algerian border, and stay with your camp guide at night.
  - Drink bottled or filtered water and go easy on raw salads for the first days; carry rehydration salts.
  - Pack for cold: desert camps and Azrou can drop below 0 C at night. Bring a warm layer, a hat, and a sleeping-bag liner.
  - Women may get verbal attention in medinas; modest dress helps, and firm 'la, shukran' (no thanks) works.
  - Stay airside at Cairo (CAI) on the EgyptAir transit, and keep the whole routing on one ticket so a missed connection is the airline's problem. EgyptAir punctuality is mediocre (~50-60% on time).
  - Enroll in STEP; carry a copy of your passport, since there are police checkpoints on rural roads.
- **Weather in late Dec:** Dry season, mostly sunny. Marrakech highs ~18-20 C, lows ~5-7 C. Ouarzazate/Dades: highs ~16-18 C, nights ~0-3 C. Merzouga/Erg Chebbi: days ~17-20 C, nights ~1-5 C (camps provide heavy blankets). Azrou/Ifrane (1,250-1,650 m): highs ~10 C, nights below freezing; snow is possible, and the macaques in snow are a bonus. Tizi n'Tichka can close briefly after snowfall. Short days: sunset ~17:45.

## Entry
- Kenya eTA $30, **etas.gov.ke only**. Türkiye: airside connections only, no visa needed. Passport 6+ mo, 2 blank pages.

## Flights
- TK10 19:45→19:00+1. TK607 **20:30 → 03:05**. 1.5h connect: tight. Missed → next night; Ol Pejeta 1n shorter.
- Return Jan 16: TK608 04:50 → IST 11:45, ~2h45 airside connect, TK9 ~14:30 → LAX ~18:15. Check times when booking; keep ≥2h connect.

## Do we need a rental car? No.
- Safari days: the camping operator's 4x4 + driver-guide is in the crew price. You never drive.
- Self-drive is possible (e.g. Roadtrip Africa Land Cruisers + rooftop tent), but **Mara conservancies don't allow self-drive vehicles**, you'd do every 4–5h drive yourselves on the left, and an 8-day self-drive package starts ~€1,730 pp: not cheaper.
- Nairobi: Uber/Bolt. Everything else in the crew vehicle.

## Road reality
- Longest days: Dec 29 (~4h), Jan 6 (4–4.5h), Jan 13 (4–4.5h). Rest day before each.
- Samburu → Nakuru and Kakamega → Mara are split with overnights (Thomson's Falls, Kericho).
- Kericho → Mara via Mulot: last hour rough; ask operator about rain.

## Weather
- Samburu hot + dry (30–35°C days). Kakamega: afternoon showers, muddy trails: rain jacket + closed shoes. Highlands cold at night.


## Fees
- KWS Nakuru $90 new vs $60 old (court case). OPC + Mara conservancies not KWS. Cashless (card/M-Pesa).

## Operator must confirm in writing
- Mara conservancy mobile camping allowed + fee. Per-day rate incl. festive days. No hidden repositioning.

## Health (CDC)
- Yellow fever recommended outside Nairobi. Malaria pills from Dec 27 to 7 days after leaving Kenya (Kakamega/west is higher risk). DEET.

## Camping
- Walk-in tents, beds, bucket shower, toilet tent. Askari at night. Laikipia/Nakuru nights ~8–12°C: fleece.

## Money/safety
- ~130 KES/$. Crisp USD for tips. Kenya Level 2: Uber/Bolt, no night walks. Plastic bags banned.

legs.detail: Overnight transatlantic, e.g. Air France/Delta LAX-CDG afternoon departure, arriving ~10:00-11:30 Dec 20. Alternatives: Iberia via MAD, or a Star Alliance ticket via FRA/MUC. Royal Air Maroc's LAX-CMN nonstop AT251 does not fly Saturdays (Sun/Tue/Fri only).
Paris-Marrakech (Air France/Transavia/Royal Air Maroc), ~2-3h connection; arrive RAK late afternoon. Then ~25 min taxi or riad pickup to the medina (~150-200 MAD).
Private driver over the High Atlas via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m). ~190 km; stops at an argan co-op and pass viewpoints, lunch at Telouet optional.
Via Ouarzazate, Skoura palmery, the Dades Valley and its gorge switchbacks to Todra Gorge. ~280 km with frequent stops.
Tinghir-Alnif-Rissani-Merzouga, ~200 km. Drop luggage at the auberge and keep a small overnight bag.
Camel trek (or 4x4 if preferred) into the Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset to the camp.
Camel or 4x4 back after the dune sunrise; rest of day easy in Merzouga.
Erfoud-Errachidia-Ziz Gorges-Midelt-Azrou, ~370 km. Break at Errachidia and lunch in Midelt; arrive at the Cedre Gouraud forest by ~15:00 for macaques. This is the longest drive, at the 5h limit.

Leave ~07:30 via Meknes on the A2/A1 toll motorways to Casablanca Mohammed V airport (~300 km), arriving ~11:00 for the 13:30 departure. Backup: Fes airport (1h15) plus a Royal Air Maroc domestic flight to CMN.
EgyptAir MS848 CMN 13:30 (T2) to CAI 20:25 (T3), A321neo, operates daily per 2026 tracker data. ~3.5h airside connection.

EgyptAir MS849 CAI 23:55 Dec 27 to NBO 04:55 Dec 28 (737-800). Some 2026 dates show a 20:55 departure instead, which would not connect, so verify the December schedule before booking. Backups: Qatar QR1396 CMN 20:50 Dec 26 to DOH 06:00, then QR1341 DOH 18:45 to NBO 23:50 Dec 27 (needs a Dec 26 Casablanca departure and drops Azrou). Or Turkish TK618 CMN Dec 26 to IST with an overnight, then TK607 IST 18:45 Dec 27 to NBO 01:25 Dec 28.

fatigue_check:
**Morocco stopover (Dec 19–28):**
Travel hours per day. Dec 19: ~10.5h flight. Dec 20: ~6h (connection + 3.5h flight + transfer). Dec 21: 0 (rest). Dec 22: ~4h road. Dec 23: ~4h road. Dec 24: ~3h road + 1.5h camel. Dec 25: ~1h (rest). Dec 26: ~5h road. Dec 27: ~3.5h road + ~5h flight + ~3.5h layover + ~5h overnight flight (arrives NBO 04:55 Dec 28). Dec 28: Nairobi rest day (Kenya plan). Pace: the ~5h max road rule is met every day, with Dec 26 at the limit. There is a rest day after the long-haul arrival (Dec 21) and after the desert (Dec 25). The weak point is Dec 26-27: two hard days back to back, ending in an overnight flight. The Dec 28 Nairobi rest day softens it. If that is too much, drop Azrou and the macaques and fly Errachidia-Casablanca on Dec 26, or overnight in Casablanca.

**Kenya (from Dec 28):**
Door-to-door travel per day:
- Dec 26–27 | flights (~13h + 6.5h) | long-haul
- Dec 28 | 20m taxi at 03:30 | REST
- Dec 29 | ~4h road | medium (after rest day)
- Dec 30 | 0 | REST
- Dec 31 | 2.5–3h road | light
- Jan 1–2 | 0 | REST ×2
- Jan 3 | ~3.5h road | medium
- Jan 4 | ~1.5h road | light
- Jan 5 | 0 | REST
- Jan 6 | 4–4.5h road | long (after rest day)
- Jan 7 | 0 | REST
- Jan 8 | 2.5–3h road | light
- Jan 9 | 3–3.5h road | medium
- Jan 10–11 | 0 | REST ×2
- Jan 12 | 0 | REST (extra Mara day)
- Jan 13 | 4–4.5h road | long (after 3 Mara rest days)
- Jan 14 | ~30m local (Hell's Gate) | REST-ish
- Jan 15 | 2.5–3h road | light
- Jan 16 | 15m + 7h + 2h45 connect + 13h45 | long-haul home (~25h, 02:45 wake)

Rules:
- **Max ~5h road:** met; longest 4–4.5h.
- **No back-to-back ≥3.5h:** met.
- **Rest days:** 9 with no transfer (incl. easy Hell's Gate day) + arrival rest day.
- 1-night stops are transit: Thomson's Falls, Kericho, airport.
- Jan 16 is the one hard day: sleep early Jan 15; sleep on the long flight.

label: Morocco Atlas + Sahara
summary: 7 nights from Marrakech over the High Atlas to the Erg Chebbi dunes (Christmas Eve in a desert camp), then north to the Middle Atlas cedar forest for Barbary macaques. Fly out from Casablanca via Cairo and land in Nairobi at about 04:55 on Dec 28. Then the Wild loop.

prelude.advisory_level: US State Dept Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (terrorism). Advisory reissued Sep 4 2026, level unchanged.
prelude.safety_short: Stable and tourist-friendly. Risks: general terrorism alert, petty theft, medina hustlers, winter mountain roads.
prelude.verdict_short: Worth it if you want a big change of scenery and culture before Kenya: Atlas passes, kasbahs, gorges, Sahara dunes and the macaques.
prelude.safety: Morocco is one of the more stable and tourist-friendly countries in Africa. The Level 2 rating reflects a general terrorism risk; terrorists may target tourist sites, transport hubs and markets. The last deadly attacks on tourists were the 2011 Marrakech cafe bombing and the 2018 killing of two hikers near Imlil. The everyday risks are petty theft, medina hustlers, and mountain driving in winter. Merzouga is close to the closed Algerian border, but the tourist dune area is routinely visited and safe.
prelude.visa: US passport: Morocco is visa-free for up to 90 days (passport must be valid 6+ months on entry; one blank page). Paris (CDG) airside transit needs no visa, and the EU EES/ETIAS systems do not apply to airside transit. Cairo transit: no Egyptian visa needed if you stay airside. Kenya eTA is still required as in the base plan, so make sure it covers a Dec 28 entry.
prelude.weather: Dry season, mostly sunny. Marrakech highs ~18-20 C, lows ~5-7 C. Ouarzazate/Dades: highs ~16-18 C, nights ~0-3 C. Merzouga/Erg Chebbi: days ~17-20 C, nights ~1-5 C (camps provide heavy blankets). Azrou/Ifrane (1,250-1,650 m): highs ~10 C, nights below freezing; snow is possible, and the macaques in snow are a bonus. Tizi n'Tichka can close briefly after snowfall. Short days: sunset ~17:45.
prelude.verdict: Worth it if you want a big change of scenery and culture before Kenya: Atlas passes, kasbahs, gorges, Sahara dunes and the macaques. The wildlife is thin next to East Africa, though: apart from the macaques and camels it is mostly birds. The main drawbacks are the long Dec 27 flight day via Cairo, with no nonstop to Nairobi, and desert nights near freezing. It adds about $2,000 pp all-in over the base trip. Checked: Level 2 advisory (Sep 4 2026), visa-free entry, the AT251 Sun/Tue/Fri pattern and MS848 (daily, 13:30-20:25) are all confirmed.
